patients.summary: Healthy 32-year-old sales representative who joined in September 2024, then had two high-speed car crashes as a restrained driver: January 2025 left hemothorax with shock, rib fractures, trauma DIC and a right femoral shaft fracture nailed in hospital; June 2026 a second left hemothorax with shock treated with a chest tube. Recovered both times; anemia followed to resolution.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller Tyler Wilder, DOB 7/2/1992, wants to set up primary care here. No current doctor nearby; last physical was a couple of years ago at a practice out of state. Membership details and fees reviewed, he signed up online while on the phone. Insurance UHC PPO through employer, card photo uploaded. New patient visit booked 9/10 at 8:00. Asked him to send a records release for his old office; form emailed.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32M here to get set up with a PCP. Feels well. No complaints today. Works as a regional sales rep, covers a big territory by car.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none, occasional ibuprofen for a sore back after long drives. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: dad with HTN since his mid-50s, well controlled. Mom hypothyroid. Nobody with bleeding problems or clots that he knows of.
SH: lives alone in Florence. Never smoked. One or two beers a week, usually less. No drugs. Plays pickup basketball when he can.
Vaccines: thinks he had a tetanus shot around 2019; records requested.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: Pleasant, fit-appearing. Vitals in flowsheet, BP fine. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abd soft, NT, no HSM. Ext warm, no edema. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright.

A/P: Healthy adult, new to practice.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipid panel today.
- One-time HIV and HCV screening, he agrees.
- PHQ-2 0.
- Flu and COVID shots when the fall supply lands, RN visit next month.
- Old records to be scanned when they arrive.
RTC 1 yr for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tyler, everything from Tuesday came back normal. Blood count is solid (hemoglobin 15.0), kidney and liver tests normal, cholesterol fine, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Prior primary care records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records from prior PCP office received by fax, 14 pages, scanned to media.
Abstracted:
- Physical 6/2022: normal exam, BP 118/74, BMI 24.9. CBC and BMP normal.
- Tdap given 4/2019.
- No chronic problems, no prescriptions on file, NKDA.
Vaccine history updated. Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after work for vaccines. Feels well, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, COVID 0.3 mL IM R deltoid, lots and VIS documented. Waited 15 min, no problems, left ambulatory.

reports.text: Portable AP chest, supine trauma film. Displaced fractures of several left lateral ribs. Large opacity layering over most of the left hemithorax, consistent with fluid. Right lung clear. Trachea midline. Heart size not well assessed on a supine film. No pneumothorax seen on this view.
reports.conclusion: Multiple left rib fractures with a large left-sided fluid collection, likely hemothorax.

reports.text: Portable AP chest after removal of the left chest tube. Left lung expanded. Small blunting of the left costophrenic angle. No pneumothorax. Left rib fractures again seen. Right lung clear.
reports.conclusion: No pneumothorax after tube removal; small left costophrenic blunting.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital Emergency Department. Date of service 01/03/2025.

CC: chest pain, short of breath after MVC.

HPI: 32-year-old man brought by EMS from a highway crash at high speed. Driver. Reports severe left-sided chest pain and trouble getting a breath since the impact.

PMH none. Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, social alcohol. Works in sales.
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroid, no bleeding or clotting disorders.

Triage: RR 28, BP 90/60, HR 120, SpO2 92% RA.

Exam: Anxious and sweaty. Left chest with diminished breath sounds and dull to percussion. Neck veins flat. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Labs: Hgb 11 (prior 15 per PCP records), Hct 33 (prior 45), WBC 12.0, plt 250.
Imaging: portable CXR with multiple left rib fractures and large left hemithorax opacification consistent with fluid.

Course: two large-bore IVs, massive transfusion protocol activated, trauma surgery at bedside. Left 28 Fr chest tube placed in the ED with immediate return of blood. Red cells and plasma running. Admitted to the trauma ICU.

Impression: traumatic left hemothorax with hypovolemic shock; multiple left rib fractures.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Trauma ICU Admission Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital Surgical/Trauma ICU. Date of service 01/03/2025, 21:00.

Reason for admission: hemorrhagic shock after MVC, worsening coagulation labs.

Interval: came up from the ED this evening after left chest tube placement and initial transfusion. Was the belted driver; airbags went off. Now restless and disoriented, pulling at lines.

Vitals: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.2 C (99.0 F).

Exam (secondary survey): bruising across the chest and abdomen. Right thigh visibly deformed, distal pulses present. Persistent oozing at IV sites. Chest tube to suction, bloody output.

Labs: Hgb 10.2, plt 55, PT 18 s, PTT 45 s, fibrinogen 150, D-dimer elevated.

Assessment:
1. Hemorrhagic (hypovolemic) shock from left traumatic hemothorax, chest tube in place.
2. Trauma-associated DIC: low platelets and fibrinogen, prolonged PT/PTT, high D-dimer, oozing.
3. Acute blood loss anemia.
4. Chest and abdominal wall contusions from blunt trauma; left rib fractures.
5. Right femur deformity, x-ray ordered.
6. Agitation/confusion, likely hypoperfusion; reassess as volume restored.

Plan: continue balanced transfusion with red cells, plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate; repeat coags every 6 h; femur x-ray and traction splint, orthopedics consult; serial chest tube output; pain control.

Addendum 23:40: femur film shows a displaced right femoral shaft fracture, closed. Splinted. Ortho to fix when coagulation allows.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Operative Report: Right Femur
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Department of Orthopaedics. Date of surgery 01/05/2025.

Preop/postop diagnosis: closed right femoral shaft fracture.
Procedure: antegrade intramedullary nailing, right femur, with proximal and distal interlocking screws.
Anesthesia: general.
Indication: closed shaft fracture in a polytrauma patient, coagulopathy now corrected (plt 138, PT 13.6, fibrinogen 236 this morning).

Findings: transverse midshaft fracture, reduced closed. Good canal fill. Fluoroscopy with restored length, alignment and rotation.
EBL 300 mL. No complications. Staples to wounds.

Postop: weight bearing as tolerated with walker. Staples out in about 2 weeks at clinic.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital Trauma Surgery. Admitted 01/03/2025, discharged 01/11/2025.

Diagnoses:
- Left traumatic hemothorax with hypovolemic shock
- Multiple left rib fractures
- Disseminated intravascular coagulation, trauma-related, resolved
- Acute posthemorrhagic anemia
- Chest wall contusion / blunt chest trauma
- Closed right femoral shaft fracture, s/p IM nail 01/05

Course: Restrained driver in a high-speed crash. Arrived in shock with a large left hemothorax; left chest tube in the ED and massive transfusion. In the ICU developed DIC with oozing and low platelets and fibrinogen, corrected with red cells, plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate by hospital day 2. Confusion cleared once perfusion improved. Right femur nailed 01/05. Chest tube output tapered and it was pulled 01/07; film afterward showed an expanded lung, no pneumothorax and slight left costophrenic blunting. Moved to the floor 01/06. Working with PT, walker.

Discharge labs: Hgb 9.1, plt 296, PT normal.

Discharge medications:
- Oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325, 1 tab every 6 h as needed for severe pain, #28
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily

Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: Orthopaedics clinic 2 weeks (staples). Trauma clinic 3-4 weeks with chest x-ray. PCP within 1 week, CBC.
Activity: WBAT right leg with walker. No driving while on opioids.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 days after discharge from the regional hospital (MVC, chest tube, femur nail). Discharge summary in chart. He is at home and managing. Pain 5/10, uses the oxycodone tab 2-3x/day. Breathing ok, no fever. Leg incisions dry. Walking to the bathroom and kitchen with walker. Taking iron, a little constipated, advised fluids and OTC stool softener. Has both meds in hand. Visit set for Thu 1/16, has a ride.

conditions.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
conditions.note: corrected in hospital, coagulation normal at discharge

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. Reviewed regional hospital records in full: high-speed MVC 1/3, L hemothorax with hemorrhagic shock, L rib fxs, chest tube, massive transfusion, trauma DIC (resolved), R femoral shaft fx s/p IM nail 1/5, d/c 1/11 with Hgb 9.1.

S: Sore, especially the left ribs with deep breaths and the right thigh at night. Using oxycodone/APAP about twice a day, down from three. Breathing easier every day. No fever, cough or bloody sputum. No bleeding or new bruising. Bowels moving with senna. Sleeping on the couch.

Meds: oxycodone/APAP 5/325 prn, ferrous sulfate 325 daily. NKDA.

O: Vitals in flowsheet. Uncomfortable moving but in no distress. Left lateral chest tube site healing, dressing clean, no drainage. Left chest tender over lateral ribs; breath sounds slightly decreased at the left base, no crackles. Heart RRR. R thigh incisions with staples, clean, no erythema, mild swelling. Calf soft, nontender both sides. Ambulating with walker.

A/P:
1. Left traumatic hemothorax, s/p chest tube: improving clinically. Trauma clinic film end of month.
2. Acute blood loss anemia: CBC and ferritin today. Continue iron.
3. R femur fx s/p nail: ortho next week for staples, PT referral to come from them.
4. Pain: taper oxycodone over the next 1-2 weeks; tylenol between doses, max 3 g/day total incl. what's in the combo.
5. DIC: resolved in hospital, no further testing planned.
No driving for now. Out of work, note given. RTC 4 wks.

documents.title: Blood count from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tyler - hemoglobin is 10.6, up from 9.1 when you left the hospital. Iron stores (ferritin 38) are on the low side, which is expected after that much blood loss, so keep taking the iron once a day. Kidney labs normal. We'll recheck at your next visit.

orders.reason: right femur fracture after IM nail

documents.title: Orthopaedics Postoperative Letter
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Outside orthopaedic group. Visit 01/22/2025.

Re: Tyler Wilder, DOB 07/02/1992

Seen 17 days after antegrade IM nailing of a closed right femoral shaft fracture. Pain improving. Walking with a walker.

Exam: incisions healed, staples removed. Thigh soft. Knee range 0-95. Neurovascularly intact distally.

X-rays right femur, 2 views: hardware intact, fracture alignment maintained, early callus.

Plan: WBAT, wean to a cane as able. Outpatient PT for gait, quad strength and knee motion. Return 3 months with x-rays.

Medications: oxycodone/acetaminophen prn, ferrous sulfate. Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Lungs are clear and well expanded. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Healing fractures of several left lateral ribs with callus. Heart size normal. Mediastinum normal.
reports.conclusion: No residual effusion. Healing left rib fractures.

documents.title: Trauma Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital Trauma Surgery Clinic. Visit 01/29/2025.

Dear colleague,

Your patient returned for follow-up after his January crash with left hemothorax and rib fractures. He is breathing comfortably at rest and on stairs, using pain medicine less. No fever or cough.

Exam: lungs clear both sides. Chest tube site healed. Rib tenderness mild.

CXR today: clear lungs, no effusion, healing left rib fractures.

The hemothorax has resolved. No further trauma clinic follow-up needed; he can return as needed. Incentive spirometer for another couple of weeks.

Medications: oxycodone/acetaminophen prn, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet

medications.sig: Take 1-2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain, max 3,000 mg per day

documents.title: Pain med refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm down to my last 3 of the oxycodone pills from the hospital. Could you send a refill? The leg is still achy at night especially after PT.

documents.title: RE: Pain med refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tyler, glad you're needing them less. Rather than refill, let's finish those last few and switch to plain acetaminophen (Tylenol) 500 mg, 1-2 tabs up to every 8 hours, no more than 3,000 mg a day. I sent a bottle to your pharmacy so you have it. Ice after therapy helps too. If the pain is clearly getting worse instead of better, call ortho or me.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after Jan MVC.
Off oxycodone since last week, acetaminophen once or twice a day. PT twice weekly started last week. Using a cane outside, nothing at home. Ribs only hurt when he laughs or sneezes. Breathing normal. Taking iron daily, mild constipation managed. Sleep improving. Mood good, bored at home. Wants to get back to work.
Trauma clinic signed off 1/29, film clear.

Exam: vitals ok, weight in flowsheet. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart RRR. R thigh incisions well healed, no swelling. Gait slightly antalgic with cane.

A/P
- Hemothorax: resolved per trauma clinic.
- Blood loss anemia: Hgb today, continue ferrous sulfate until repeat in ~2 mo.
- R femur fx: PT per ortho, ortho visit April.
- Work: remains out; disability paperwork when it comes.
RTC prn, labs April.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient physical therapy clinic. Evaluation 02/19/2025.

Dx: s/p IM nail right femoral shaft fracture 01/05/2025.
Patient goal: return to work driving a sales territory, back to basketball.

Objective: R knee AROM 0-110. Quad strength 4-/5 R, 5/5 L. Hip abductors 4/5 R. Gait with single-point cane, decreased stance time R. Timed up and go 11 s.

Assessment: expected deficits after femur fixation, good rehab potential.
Plan: 2x/week for 8 weeks, progressive strengthening, gait training, wean cane. HEP issued.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Orthopaedics Follow-up Letter
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Outside orthopaedic group. Visit 04/16/2025.

Re: Tyler Wilder

Now about 3.5 months after IM nailing of the right femur. Walking without a cane, no pain at rest, mild ache after long days. Finishing PT.

Exam: normal gait. Knee 0-130. Quad strength nearly symmetric. No tenderness at the fracture site.

X-rays right femur, 2 views: bridging callus across the fracture on both views, hardware intact.

Impression: united right femoral shaft fracture.

Plan: full activity as tolerated; may return to work including driving, as he is off opioids. Finish remaining PT visits. Hardware stays unless it bothers him. Follow up as needed.

Medications: acetaminophen prn, ferrous sulfate. Allergies: NKDA.
